use: The overall situation or what's going on: ima no joukyou (the current situation).

example.romaji: ima dou iu joukyou na no?
example.english: So what's going on right now?

examplePolite.romaji: ima dou iu joukyou desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今どういう状況ですか?

notes: Joutai is the condition of one person or thing; joukyou is the wider picture.

use: A way to get something done: ~ houhou ga nai (there's no way to ~), ii houhou (a good way).

example.romaji: hoka ni houhou wa nai no?

examplePolite.romaji: hoka ni houhou wa arimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 他に方法はありませんか?

notes: Yarikata is the casual 'way of doing it'. Shikata ga nai = it can't be helped.

use: How a person or thing is doing: kanja no joutai (the patient's condition), kuruma no joutai.

example.romaji: konna joutai de shigoto nante muri da yo
example.ja: こんな状態で仕事なんて無理だよ
example.english: There's no way I can work in this state.

examplePolite.romaji: konna joutai de shigoto wa muri desu
examplePolite.ja: こんな状態で仕事は無理です
examplePolite.english: I can't work in this condition.

notes: Sounds close to joukyou (situation); joutai is about how one thing is doing.

use: Usually iwakan ga aru: something feels wrong or not quite right, in a situation or in your body.

example.romaji: atarashii megane, mada chotto iwakan ga aru
example.ja: 新しいメガネ、まだちょっと違和感がある
example.english: My new glasses still feel a bit weird.

examplePolite.romaji: atarashii megane, mada chotto iwakan ga arimasu
examplePolite.ja: 新しいメガネ、まだちょっと違和感があります
examplePolite.english: My new glasses still feel a little strange.

notes: Also for stories or behavior that don't add up: kare no hanashi ni iwakan ga aru (something's off about his story).

use: Being conscious (ishiki ga nai, he's out cold) and being aware of something (~ o ishiki suru).

example.ja: 彼、まだ意識が戻らない

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa mada ishiki ga modorimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼はまだ意識が戻りません

notes: Ishiki shiteru = be conscious of someone, often a hint of a crush. Muishiki ni = without thinking.

use: Emotions as a whole, often about showing or holding them in; 'how I feel' right now is kimochi.

example.romaji: kare wa kanjou o kao ni dasanai
example.ja: 彼は感情を顔に出さない
example.english: He doesn't let his feelings show on his face.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kanjou o kao ni dashimasen
examplePolite.ja: 彼は感情を顔に出しません
examplePolite.english: He doesn't let his feelings show on his face.

notes: Kanjouteki ni naru = get emotional. Same sound as kanjou, the bill at a restaurant.

use: Physical sensation (te no kankaku ga nai, no feeling in my hand) and a feel for things.

example.romaji: samusugite yubi no kankaku ga nai
example.ja: 寒すぎて指の感覚がない
example.english: It's so cold I can't feel my fingers.

examplePolite.romaji: samusugite yubi no kankaku ga arimasen
examplePolite.ja: 寒すぎて指の感覚がありません
examplePolite.english: It's so cold I can't feel my fingers.

notes: Kankaku de = by feel, by instinct. Emotions are kanjou, not kankaku.

use: Almost always ~ yokan ga suru: iya na yokan ga suru (I've got a bad feeling).

example.romaji: nanka iya na yokan ga suru
example.ja: なんか嫌な予感がする
example.english: I've got a bad feeling about this.

examplePolite.romaji: nan da ka iya na yokan ga shimasu
examplePolite.ja: なんだか嫌な予感がします
examplePolite.english: I have a bad feeling about this.

notes: Ii yokan = a good feeling about it. Yokan ga ataru = your hunch turns out right.
